key_features.classic_presentation: UTI: dysuria, frequency, urgency, suprapubic discomfort. Pyelonephritis: flank pain, fever, chills, nausea/vomiting, costovertebral angle tenderness. Pyelonephritis is upper tract infection requiring urgent treatment.
key_features.typical_demographics: Females >> males (except elderly). Risk factors: sexual activity, pregnancy, diabetes, catheters.
key_features.pathophysiology_brief: Bacterial infection of bladder (cystitis) or kidney (pyelonephritis). E. coli most common (80%).

diagnostic_questions.context: Dysuria is hallmark of UTI. Present in 90% of cystitis.
Frequency and urgency very common in cystitis.
Fever indicates pyelonephritis (upper tract). Cystitis typically no fever.
Common in pyelonephritis, uncommon in simple cystitis.

differential_diagnosis.key_difference: Colicky pain, radiation to groin, no dysuria typically

red_flags.action: High risk for preterm labor - urgent hospitalization

typical_management: Cystitis: oral antibiotics (nitrofurantoin, Bactrim). Pyelonephritis: may need IV antibiotics, admission. Pregnant: always admit.
disposition: Cystitis: outpatient. Pyelonephritis: many require admission, especially if can't tolerate PO, pregnant, or toxic-appearing.
patient_education: UTI is bacterial infection of urinary tract. Bladder infection (cystitis) treated with oral antibiotics. Kidney infection (pyelonephritis) is more serious and may need hospitalization.
